primitives.name: Want Generation Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the first place, the economic process produces wants as well as goods to satisfy existing wants, and the amount of social energy devoted to the former and neglected phase of activity is very large and constantly growing.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W(t)': 'dimensionless want intensity at time t', 'E(t)': 'social energy devoted to want creation at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Want generation is exogenous to consumption, grows exponentially with time, and is proportional to available social energy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E(t) approaches zero, W(t) stabilizes or decays.

layer2.mapping: Recursive utility function where W(t) drives U(W(t)) = ∫u(w(s))ds, influencing production decisions.
layer2.telemetry: Observable: consumer survey data on desire intensity; measurable: GDP growth rate vs. want index.

primitives.name: Capital Accumulation Structure
primitives.verbatim_quote: The most important of these from our point of view and at the same time the one easiest to discuss intelligently is the accumulation of capital.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K(t)': 'capital stock at time t (monetary units)', 'I(t)': 'investment flow at time t (monetary units per period)'}
primitives.assumptions: Capital accumulation follows a deterministic flow governed by savings rate and productivity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When I(t) < 0, K(t) declines; when I(t) = 0, K(t) remains constant.

layer2.mapping: Capital stock K(t) maps to state vector in GSE transition system, where I(t) acts as control input.
layer2.telemetry: Observable: fixed asset investment; measurable: net capital formation rate.

primitives.name: Consumption Sacrifice Ratio
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is true to a great and ever-increasing degree that consumption is sacrificed to increased production.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C(t)': 'consumption level at time t (goods units)', 'P(t)': 'production level at time t (goods units)', 'R(t)': 'sacrifice ratio C(t)/P(t)'}
primitives.assumptions: R(t) increases monotonically with technological advancement and societal development.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If R(t) > 1, consumption exceeds production; if R(t) < 1, production exceeds consumption.

layer2.mapping: R(t) defines a dynamic constraint in GSI's resource allocation model, affecting posterior beliefs about future utility.
layer2.telemetry: Observable: household saving rates; measurable: ratio of consumption to gross domestic product.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that economic systems evolve beyond simple consumption-driven models into complex feedback loops involving want generation, capital accumulation, and consumption sacrifice. Want generation introduces a non-linear feedback mechanism where new desires fuel further production, creating a self-reinforcing cycle. Capital accumulation becomes a structural kernel, representing the material basis for future production capacity. Consumption sacrifice reflects a shift in value orientation—where individuals prioritize wealth accumulation over immediate gratification. These three primitives form a triadic structure: W(t) → K(t) → R(t), each influencing the others through recursive utility functions. The failure mode occurs when one component breaks down—e.g., if want generation stagnates, capital accumulation halts, and consumption sacrifice loses meaning. Dualities emerge between internal desire and external production, between short-term consumption and long-term investment, and between individual behavior and systemic dynamics.
